arguments.heading: What happened at the argument
paragraphs: Mr. Richie argued the NLRB Act clearly states a quorum of three is required at all times.
Mr. Katyal argued section 153(b) permits delegation of any or all board powers to three or more members.
Justice Scalia questioned whether the side that brought the case's argument relies on the board's inability to act when membership falls below three.
Justice Scalia asked if the board can pay salaries when its quorum disappears.

sections.heading: What this case is about
paragraphs: The NLRB Act requires a quorum of three members. the side that brought the case argues this rule is absolute. the opposing side argues the board can delegate full powers to a three-member group.

sections.heading: What each side wants
paragraphs: the side that brought the case wants the Court to hold that the NLRB cannot issue decisions with only two members.
